description: Spellings the polytonic Modern Greek word list (export_mg_polytonic.py) admitted but a recorded review rejected, read together with data/hunspell_grc_spelling_review.json. respelling: a word written with an accent type or iota subscript it does not have, where the slice's own commoner spelling is the right one. structural: words run together, or a contextual twin the word cannot have. Misspellings in the breathing alone are left to the exporter's breathing rule, and a respelling rare enough beside its correct spelling to its rule 4.
method: An adversarial review of the whole 17,789-entry list flagged every entry whose breathing, accent-type or iota-subscript twin is five times commoner in the slice, or at least as common and in grc, and judged each from its corpus sentences; a second review checked the judgments. Listed are the misspellings no rule rejects, with ὥρες, which the same scan flagged once the list was rebuilt with the breathing rule and the per-case thresholds. Kept although flagged: the variants the reviews accepted (θέσῃ, the subjunctive beside the noun θέση; πᾷς; τρομερᾶς; ἀκριβῆς, the feminine genitive; κορῶνα), and ποιητῆ, the genitive beside the accusative ποιητή. Some acute spellings the second review held to be a demoticist convention (μήνας, χειμώνα, ἀγώνα) are listed: the slice writes the circumflex spelling at least five times as often, and a keyboard writes that one. Counts are tokens in the language model's training split of the slice.
